purpose: Broadly randomized pretraining data for a world model (deformation-focused). Not a calibration of the experimental chip; not a replacement for the frozen HF/LF science path.
base: Self-contained since 2026-11-06 (user decision): a run reads only this file, and every value in it is the value in effect. The frozen files configs/frozen/contact_policy.json and contact_revision.json, on which this tier was first layered, are kept as evidence and no longer read.
contact_values: Contact-step tolerances and gates. hard_geometry_m (1 nm), contact_overlap_m (0.01R), contact_correction_m (0.1R, applied to the actual step displacement), dual_negative_N and force_residual_atol_N are the frozen baseline values (configs/frozen/contact_policy.json). mobility_residual_m, primal_violation_m, complementarity_equivalent_gap_m, actual_geometry_complementarity_m and force_residual_rtol were loosened at the tier admission from the frozen 1e-13 m, 1e-12 m, 1e-12 m, 1e-11 m and 1e-8 to observation scale (evidence/pretrain_tier_20261102/). max_sequential_qp 1 (frozen 5, contact_revision.json): one linearization per step since 2026-11-06. Since 2026-11-06 the gates are recorded, not enforced.

tier_rules.qp_solver: Every constrained contact QP is solved by DAQP 0.11 (native/daqp_qp.cpp, sources DAQP_DIR, MIT licence; inside native/contact_step.cpp for the compiled step, contact.DaqpQP for the Python step), in least-distance form built from the step's Cholesky factor of A (since 2026-11-06: DAQP gets no Hessian, so it skips a dense factorization and transformation that took about 90% of the contact step; same solutions and iterations, 122-bubble runs 13.1 s -> 8.5 s, evidence/daqp_ldp_20261106/), warm-started with the pairs active in the previous DAQP solve (they start in its working set; since 2026-11-07 loaded as one block: their table M_A M_A' in one matrix product, factorized at once and written into DAQP's workspace, a pivoted factorization leaving out contacts that depend on the others; same solutions and iterations, 122-bubble steps 16.8 -> 12.3 ms, evidence/daqp_block_warm_start_20261107/), default DAQP tolerances (primal 1e-6 in units of R = 1.8e-12 m), iteration limit daqp.iteration_limit; its solution is used if DAQP reports optimal (gates only recorded), otherwise the run stops. Since 2026-11-06 (user decisions). Before that day the frozen active set solved the QP and a fallback took the steps where it failed: OSQP (eps 1e-9, later 1e-7), which did not converge on the dense 3D networks of random starts (~3N-6 linearly dependent contacts, active set ending on active_set_inconsistent_equalities) and stopped 76- and 122-bubble runs within 0.1 s, then qpOASES; then qpOASES for every constrained step (runs 1.75-1.77x faster at 76 and 122 bubbles); then DAQP, about 3x faster than qpOASES on the same 397 QPs, same solutions (evidence/fixed_step_dt_20261106/, evidence/qpoases_fallback_20261106/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision), evidence/qpoases_contact_20261106/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision), evidence/daqp_contact_20261106/).
tier_rules.contact_correction: 0.1R limit applies to the largest actual bubble displacement of the step instead of the push cancelled by contacts

random_actions.use: Since 2026-11-06 (user decision) every run draws its own actions (control.random_actions): the run is cut into segments of segment_s (config "action_segment_s" may change it; duration_s must be a whole number of segments, at most max_segments); in each segment every channel is on with probability channel_on_probability, an open channel gets an amplitude uniform in [0, max_source_amplitude_Pa_equivalent), a closed one 0; phases uniform in [0, 2 pi), the frequency uniform in frequency_range_Hz of this block (2-3 MHz; since 2026-11-08 the run may use 2-10 MHz, the top-level frequency_range_Hz, but random actions still draw from 2-3 MHz). The config must give the seed "action_seed"; the same seed gives the same actions. The predefined action table (inputs/actions.json, kept as data) and handwritten controls (config "action", "control") were removed the same day.

pattern_actions.use: Since 2026-11-08 (user decision) a share of the runs (control.pattern_run on the action seed) does not use random_actions but control.pattern_actions: the standing-wave zero line or zero point of the four discs first passes through a reference point, then turns, moves, bends and changes between line and point smoothly at random (knots every knot_interval_s, linear in between, segments of random_actions.segment_s, at most max_segments). One frequency per run, uniform in frequency_range_Hz; the largest channel of the run at the source cap. "action_kind" "pattern" (drawn, for pretraining): the reference point is the channel centre, the commands do not depend on where the cluster is, the start stays random and the field away from the centre is used as it is. "pattern_local" (only by config, to check simulation against real experiments): the reference point is the start cluster's centre, the commands follow the actual field there. A config may also set "random". The adhesion is that of every run (adhesion.force_range_N).

random_state.use: Since 2026-11-06 (user decision) every run draws its own start (initial_conditions.random_start): a three-dimensional irregular cluster grown on the spot (irregular_cluster_3d: ballistic aggregation with partial restructuring) with a bubble count drawn as an integer uniformly in bubble_count_range and an aspect drawn uniformly in aspect_range, turned to a uniform random orientation and placed with its centre uniform over the admissible part of the channel: along the whole axis and over the whole cross-section, with every bubble surface at least wall_margin_m from the bore wall and the end planes. The config must give the seed "state_seed"; the same seed gives the same start. Handwritten "state" and "offset_m" were removed the same day; the stored single-layer clusters (inputs/pretrain_irregular_states.h5) are no longer used. Since 2026-11-07 the bubbles of a start differ in size (radius below).

radius.use: Since 2026-11-07 (user decision) bubbles differ in size: every bubble of a start gets a radius from a log-normal distribution with median median_m and geometric standard deviation sigma_g, drawn per run uniformly in sigma_g_range (a config may fix it with "radius_sigma_g"; 1 makes every bubble median_m and gives the start of the same seed before this date bit for bit), truncated to range_m (drawn again outside it), the radius range of the shell data (apecss_response.shell_vs_radius). The sizes have a random stream of their own (initial_conditions.random_start), the cluster is grown with them (contact at the sum of the two radii). Radii are recorded in task.start.radii_m and trajectory.h5 radii_m.

adhesion.use: Since 2026-11-08 (user decision) every run has the same kind of adhesion, independent of the sound: without "adhesion_force_N" in its config a run draws one log-uniformly from force_range_N, on its own stream of the state seed (numpy default_rng([state_seed, 2]), workflows.f10ag.contact_terms), weak enough not to keep clusters from taking a shape (evidence/morph_sheet_20261108/). A config may give adhesion_force_N; 0 turns adhesion off. calibrated_force_N is the force calibrated against the A/B softness at 2.5 MHz (until 2026-11-08 the default force_N, with force_range_N [2.7e-10, 9e-10]); it is kept for reference and is not used by default. Until 2026-11-07 the force was coefficient 1.4e-17 N/(Pa-eq)^2 (range 7.5e-18 to 2.5e-17) x the square of the run's largest single-channel amplitude; calibrated_force_N and the former range are those values at the 6000 Pa-eq source cap.

apecss_response.use: Default since 2026-11-04 (policy "response": "apecss"); the frozen response tables ("table") were removed from this tier on 2026-11-05 (user decision). APECSS sources from config "apecss_dir" or the APECSS_DIR environment variable; config "apecss_threads" sets only the thread count (default threads: 8 from 2026-11-04, 16 since 2026-11-07 by user decision, the physical cores of the server's Ryzen 9 7950X; results do not depend on it, evidence/pair_forces_compiled_20261107/). The library is compiled once per source set into build/apecss/ (bubble_response.cached_apecss_library).

shell_vs_radius.use: Since 2026-11-07 (user decision) the bubble of radius R has the case above except elasticity = max(elasticity_N_m + elasticity_N_m_per_um (R - radius_m) [um], elasticity_floor_N_m) and shell viscosity = shell_viscosity_kg_s x 10^(shell_viscosity_decades_per_um (R - radius_m) [um]) (bubble_response.shell_parameters): the slopes of least-squares fits to the SonoVue data of Tu et al. 2009 (J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 126, 2954, Fig. 4, linearized Marmottant model, read off the figure, about +-10%), the lines through the case at radius_m, the floor Tu's smallest elasticities (0.8-1.0 um). Evidence: evidence/f2_physics_check_20261107/.

apecss_response.bubble_source: The ten bubble, shell and liquid parameters of the APECSS case admitted in inputs/response/2400000/PHYSICS_GATE.json (response.case, PASS), copied unchanged on 2026-11-06 (user decision) so that a run no longer reads that file; the file stays as evidence. Historical radius-dependent SonoVue parameters, elasticity multiplier 1.0; the initial surface tension 0.036 N/m is a hypothesis, not a calibration. They do not depend on the frequency: APECSS runs at each segment's frequency.

reasons.pattern_actions: User decision 2026-11-08: pretraining data should contain smooth changes of shape, like a sheet of bubbles turning, moving or bending with a slowly changing standing wave (evidence/rotate_sheet_20261108/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision), evidence/morph_sheet_20261108/ (part 1, the sheet changes, deleted 2026-11-09, user decision)), in half of the runs, at 3-10 MHz, where bubbles gather on the zero set (evidence/sculpt_4pzt_20261108/). Independent random segments almost never give a zero line: one exists only when the two pairs are exactly in phase or opposite, so the actions follow the pattern family itself (control.pattern_actions). The family keeps the size of the pressure gradient at the zero set fixed, so the push towards it does not change while the pattern changes. knot_interval_s 1-6 s gives changes of direction of about 17 deg/s on average, around where a 250-bubble sheet stops following (3.5 deg/s follows, 14 deg/s just, 56 deg/s lags, evidence/rotate_sheet_20261108/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision)), so the data hold both following and lagging. node_offset_max_m 16 um: with knots 1-6 s apart the nodes then move about 3 um/s typically (up to about 30 um/s), where the sheet stops following a moving node (0.8 um/s follows, 3.1 um/s just, 12.5 um/s lags, evidence/morph_sheet_20261108/ (part 1, the sheet changes, deleted 2026-11-09, user decision)); a quarter wavelength (37-125 um at 10-3 MHz, tried first) moved the nodes at 8-23 um/s typically, and in the four test runs the zero set mostly ran away from the cluster (evidence/pattern_actions_20261108/). A node offset of one pair bends the zero line through the cluster. zero_set_weights: at the knots a line half of the time, a point a quarter, in between a quarter; the zero line stays exact while two neighbouring knots are both lines (about a quarter of the time), elsewhere only a point is exactly zero, with a nearly zero valley along the former line while phi is small. Reference point (user decision 2026-11-08): for pretraining the commands do not depend on the cluster's position (channel centre), and a cluster away from the centre meets the field of the pattern there as it is; designing the commands from the field at the cluster (pattern_local) is kept only for checking simulation against experiments. Away from the channel centre along x the Y discs' waves arrive obliquely, the phase between the pairs changes across a cluster and no exact zero line exists there: with the commands designed at each of 200 random starts, those within 4 mm of the centre (19%) got a zero line within 3-5% of the local |p| (median), those 8-16 mm away (55%) only a valley (19-33%) (evidence/pattern_actions_20261108/).
reasons.random_state: Random starts for world-model pretraining data (user decision 2026-11-06): the camera sees silhouettes of three-dimensional clusters, so the clusters are three-dimensional and their bubble count (any integer; 64-255 since 2026-11-08, user decision, 16-128 before), aspect (1.0-1.4, the range of the earlier stored clusters), orientation and position are all drawn per run, over the whole channel model. A 50 um margin to the wall and the ends keeps runs from starting at the 2R wall guard and stopping at once; the top holes are ignored, as by the wall guard.
reasons.random_actions: Random actions for pretraining a world model that is later trained jointly with reinforcement learning (user decision 2026-11-06). Fixed segments (0.1 s) act as a fixed control interval and match the world model's 0.1 s prediction step. Channels are switched on and off at random (each on with probability 0.5) rather than drawing all four amplitudes uniformly: uniform amplitudes are practically never zero, so single channels (a wave pushing from one side), opposite pairs (a standing wave), three channels and all off (the cluster evolving under its own interactions) would almost never occur, although they are physically distinct and a policy may choose them. With 0.5 the number of open channels 0/1/2/3/4 occurs in the ratio 1:4:6:4:1.
reasons.tolerances: Residual tolerances tied to the observation scale (a camera pixel is about 600 nm) instead of 1e-13 m; the strict tier stalls on degenerate contact networks (evidence: STRICT_VS_PRETRAIN.json).
reasons.stepping: Fixed step since 2026-11-06 (user decision; the external control interval is 0.1 s): every run, control segment and save interval is a whole number of fixed_step_s (a run may set "fixed_step_s"); each step has one linearization of the contacts (max_sequential_qp 1, overrides) and is always accepted; the gates are only recorded. The run stops only when the constraint problem is not solved (active set, then OSQP), on a real overlap above hard_geometry_m or a contact outside the candidates, or at the wall guard. Reason: with the adaptive control, a step whose force-balance gate (1e-10 m) failed was relinearized, and the relinearized steps made the formed 32-bubble cluster turn 31-807% too fast at 0.75-3% R per step, while one linearization at fixed steps stays within 0.06% up to 10% R per step (7 ms) and within 12 nm of the reference (evidence/step_sweep_20261106/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision), evidence/step_sweep_once_20261106/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision)). The adaptive control (displacement target, halving, rejection memory, step_control 2026-11-02) was removed. fixed_step_s 1 ms: four random 3D starts (20, 50, 76, 122 bubbles, random actions, 0.5 s, NNLS fallback as a test patch) against 0.1 ms; 1 ms is the largest step within 1 px (0.6 um) for every start that does not rearrange (<= 0.47 px), 2 ms ejected a bubble from the 76-bubble cluster (1.6 R per step, 180 px); the 122-bubble start rearranges differently at every step size, including 0.2 vs 0.1 ms, and its centroid (<= 0.07 px), shape and top-view aspect differences at 1 ms equal those at 0.2 ms. 1 ms was also the cheapest (larger steps enlarge the candidate set). With the former OSQP fallback the 76- and 122-bubble starts stopped within 0.1 s at 1 ms (evidence/fixed_step_dt_20261106/; since 2026-11-06 qpOASES, tier_rules.qp_fallback).
reasons.source_cap: 6000 Pa-equivalent since 2026-11-04 (was 3000, the largest amplitude of the prototype comparisons), so clusters reach the A/B cluster speeds: one channel at 6000 gives at most 11.7 kPa at the bubbles, four in phase 39.1 kPa, inside the 40 kPa table; 6000 Pa-eq reproduces 3000 Pa-eq four times faster within 0.09 px; protocol and random-action runs at the cap pass (evidence/pretrain_source_cap_20261104/ADMISSION.json). The response-table domain check still fails outside the table. The frozen HF/LF cap stays 1500.
reasons.wall_guard: No wall contact is modelled in this tier; runs stop 2R from the lumen wall or end.
reasons.frequency: Since 2026-11-09 (user decision) frequency_range_Hz is 0.5-10 MHz: low-frequency runs at 0.5-2 MHz with the existing model (free-field water, carried APECSS response), after the experiment showed bubble motion below 2 MHz; random actions still draw from 2-3 MHz. Earlier: since 2026-11-05 (user decision): any drive frequency in frequency_range_Hz, 2-3 MHz (the adjustable range of the experimental drive) until 2026-11-08, 2-10 MHz since then (user decision 2026-11-08, the signal generator's limit; random actions still draw from 2-3 MHz, random_actions.frequency_range_Hz); since 2026-11-06 each segment may set its own (segment key "frequency", default the run frequency). The FNM disc field and the carried APECSS response are both computed at the segment frequency, so no response table or field cache limits it; before, only the registered 2.4/2.5/2.6 MHz were admitted. The APECSS case (bubble and shell) is the same at every frequency. At a switch every bubble continues with its radial and gas state at the new frequency (native/apecss_harmonics.c carried_set_frequency; every call starts at drive phase 0 after whole cycles, so the drive phase is continuous; the settling decay rate is measured again, at least three cycles) and the disc model is rebuilt at the new frequency on the same device. trajectory.h5 action_* hold the command in effect from each saved time on. The frozen HF/LF path keeps 2.4/2.5/2.6 MHz. Up to 10 MHz the disc field uses the registered quadrature orders (acoustics.DIRECT_QUADRATURE_ORDERS) and the carried APECSS response settles with the check of 2026-11-08 (native/apecss_harmonics.c: changes measured against at least FUND_FLOOR, and a change below tol (1 - Q_MAX) / Q_MAX accepted without a measured decay rate; before, bubbles at a pressure node and bubbles at 7-10 MHz could run to max_cycles, APECSS_CARRIED_NOT_CONVERGED); runs at 2-3 MHz are unchanged bit for bit (evidence/sculpt_4pzt_20261108/).
reasons.apparatus: Chip geometry file (relative to the repository root) for workflows.f10ag.pretrain_context. Since 2026-11-09 (user decision) the Y-channel chip of the experiment: inputs/apparatus_y_channel.json, a square-section Y channel (trunk 179 um, branches 120.5/113.3 um, 48.8 deg between them) in an 18.6 x 14.4 x 9.75 mm PDMS block with 5.4 mm square PZTs at the side-face centres, level with the channel (geometry.YChannelCavity, acoustics.WaterSquares / gpu.GPUWaterSquares). inputs/apparatus_snapshot.json is the earlier chip (straight 1.6 mm lumen, 7 mm discs) that every run before 2026-11-09 used; set it here to reproduce them. Runs record the file and its SHA-256 in task.apparatus. Evidence: evidence/y_channel_chip_20261109/.
reasons.field: Default since 2026-11-04 (user decision): "direct_gpu", the FNM disc field evaluated at the bubbles on the GPU (gpu.GPUWaterDiscs, config "device", default cuda:0); needs Warp and CUDA. "direct" is the same field on the CPU. The stored cubic cache ("cache") was removed from this tier on 2026-11-05 (user decision); runs made with it (all runs before 2026-11-04 without a "field" key) need the code of that date to be reproduced. Same numbers: at 64 cluster states and 31,488 lumen points the GPU and CPU field and forces differ by at most 7e-14 (relative); three whole runs (protocol 32 and 128 bubbles, random actions 32 bubbles) give the same steps and positions within 4e-18 m. Speed: with the loop kernel alone those runs took 1.2-1.4x longer than with the CPU field (a call of 32-128 points is dominated by the kernel run and the GPU clocks down between calls). Since the same day GPUWaterDiscs.evaluate uses the node-thread kernel (one thread per quadrature node) up to gpu.NODE_THREAD_MAX_POINTS = 512 points per call and the loop kernel above; the same runs now take as long as with the CPU field (32.0/32.0 s, 87.9/85.1 s, 23.4/22.7 s), a 32-point call takes 0.34 ms against 0.66 ms on the CPU, and large calls stay 40x faster. Evidence: evidence/pretrain_gpu_field_20261104/, evidence/gpu_field_node_threads_20261104/.
reasons.propagation_delay: Bubble-bubble coupling (collective closure, pair closure and F2) keeps the propagation delay of the radiated monopole field, exp(-i k d) and (1 + i k d) in its gradient, k from the same water model as the field. The instantaneous form is valid only for k d << 1 (wavelength 0.6 mm at 2.5 MHz). Checked against APECSS's own interacting bubbles (fundamental oscillation, linear regime): instantaneous (IC) interactions reproduce the old form, quasi-acoustic (QA) interactions the delayed form within 0.07-0.57% for spread states where the old form is off by 42-109% (evidence/collective_flip_20261103/); the force term against a numerical gradient of the delayed field (tests/test_pretrain.py). Compact clusters change little (k d <= 0.2). A run may set "propagation_delay": false to reproduce runs made before 2026-11-03.
reasons.adhesion: Phenomenological short-range surface adhesion F = adhesion_force_N (1 - h / adhesion_range_m)^2 for surface gaps h < adhesion_range_m (microbubble.forces.adhesion_forces). Since 2026-11-04 on by default through the calibrated coefficient; since 2026-11-07 (user decision) a fixed force that does not depend on the drive (see adhesion.use); "adhesion_force_N": 0 reproduces runs before 2026-11-04. Motivated by user observations (clusters stay together after the ultrasound is switched off; real clusters deform about 40x less per pixel moved than collective-coupling clusters); no published bubble-bubble adhesion strength exists for SonoVue, so the force is calibrated against the A/B softness metric. The 0.2 um range is wider than molecular adhesion so the 3% R step control resolves it. Runs with it carry the PHENOMENOLOGICAL_ADHESION label. Calibration (evidence/adhesion_calibration_20261104/, collective coupling with delay, X- held, AG32 started as a round cluster): adhesion_force_N of (3e-11 to 1e-10) x (A / 2000 Pa-eq)^2, A the per-channel source level, stops splitting and brings the shape change per pixel moved to 0.0022-0.0048 (A/B 0.0018; without adhesion about 0.07); clusters still elongate to aspect 1.3-1.5 under a sustained push (A/B 1.12). Started from the registered gapped arrays, clusters lock in elongated (aspect 2-2.3). With the default coefficient the formed initial clusters (inputs/pretrain_formed_states.h5) never split; at 3000 Pa-eq (43 px/s) their shape change per pixel looked like A/B, but that was the pixel floor of the metric. At matched speed (6000 Pa-eq, 172 px/s) they change shape about 3x less than A/B (0.0075 against 0.024 per 0.1 s; rigid floor 0.003), and 0.1-1x the coefficient gives the same: the formed clusters are too rigid for a reason other than adhesion (evidence/softness_matched_speed_20261104/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision)). Fixed force since 2026-11-07: the coefficient made the adhesion of a whole run follow its largest single-channel amplitude, so a run with every channel off had none (although the motivating observation is clusters staying together with the ultrasound off), and a strong later segment raised the adhesion of the earlier ones. With a standing-wave node at the cluster the acoustic forces nearly vanish and the fixed adhesion alone holds the cluster (evidence/node_test_20261107/). Runs whose largest single-channel amplitude A is below the cap now have (6000 Pa-eq / A)^2 times the former adhesion (evidence/adhesion_fixed_20261107/). Since 2026-11-08 (user decision: adhesion may be lowered and must not be what keeps shapes from changing; every run the same kind of adhesion, independent of the sound, drawn from one range; pretraining values within the range validated by tests) every run without adhesion_force_N draws it log-uniformly from force_range_N 1e-14-1e-12 N. A centred 128-bubble start under one pair at the cap flattens onto the node plane as without adhesion with 1e-14 and 1e-13 N (0.95-1.20 as far at 3.4, 6.0 and 9.375 MHz), 0.63-0.95 as far with 1e-12 N, hardly with 1e-11 N and above (0.07-0.26); at 6.0 and 9.375 MHz the range ends hold at 64 and 255 bubbles too (0.52-1.01). Not validated at 2-3.3 MHz: there 64-251-bubble starts with 1e-14 or 1e-12 N break into 3-13 pieces and bubbles move up to about 4 R in a 1 ms step (30-90% of the steps above 0.1 R; the 1 ms and 0.5 ms runs part by 0.7-22 um, 0.1 ms still does not converge); 1e-10 N and the calibrated force keep them whole and calm at 1 ms. User decision pending (evidence/morph_sheet_20261108/, evidence/pretrain_ranges_20261108/). The calibrated 5.04e-10 N holds every cluster at 7-10 MHz; with the weak range the 2.5 MHz softness no longer follows the A/B calibration above.
reasons.response: Default since 2026-11-04 (user decision): "apecss", every bubble carries its own APECSS radial state from step to step (bubble_response.CarriedApecssResponse, settings in apecss_response); needs the APECSS sources (config "apecss_dir" or APECSS_DIR) and gcc. "table" (the frozen response tables) was removed from this tier on 2026-11-05 (user decision); runs made with it (all runs before 2026-11-04 without a "response" key) need the code of that date to be reproduced. One bubble from rest: the fundamental agrees with the 2.4/2.6 MHz tables within 0.06% and with the 2.5 MHz table within 2.1%; the 2.5 MHz table overstates the second harmonic about 17x near 1 kPa (no table points between 0.1 Pa and 20 kPa), APECSS does not, and APECSS has no 12 kPa limit at 2.4/2.6 MHz. Whole runs (protocol 32 and 128 bubbles, random actions 32 bubbles) all pass; cluster travel differs by 0.2%, 4.5% and 0.04%, aspect ratios are the same; with one APECSS thread and a compile at every run start, runs took 1.5-1.85x as long as with the tables (about 1.1 cycles per bubble and step); with the defaults since the same day (apecss_response.threads 8, library compiled once per source set into build/apecss/) they take 1.10-1.13x as long, with trajectories identical to the single-thread runs. Evidence: evidence/pretrain_apecss_response_20261104/.
reasons.contact: Default since 2026-11-04 (user decision): "compiled", each contact step and its resistance matrix in one call into native/contact_step.cpp (contact.CompiledContactStep), compiled once per source set into build/contact/ (contact.cached_contact_library; needs g++ and the Eigen 3.4 headers, /usr/include/eigen3). Same formulas, tolerances and gates as sparse_resistance + sparse_sequential_step; only the linear algebra differs (sparse Cholesky for SuperLU). Since 2026-11-06 both solve every constrained QP with DAQP (tier_rules.qp_solver; the library also holds native/daqp_qp.cpp and the DAQP sources); until then they used the same active set (a complete orthogonal decomposition for gelsy in the compiled step) and the compiled step handed failed steps to the Python one. "python" (those two functions) is kept unchanged; runs without a "contact" key made before 2026-11-04 used it, so set it to reproduce them bit for bit. Same results: 20,651 recorded steps of three runs give the same accept/reject decision and positions within 5.4e-20 m; whole runs (protocol 32 and 128 bubbles, random actions 32) take the same steps, positions within 1.7e-14 m. Speed: per step 3.3-3.4x faster at 32 bubbles and 1.24x at 128 bubbles (there a 342 x 342 least squares dominates), whole runs 1.42x, 1.09x and 1.49x faster. Evidence: evidence/contact_speed_20261104/ (deleted 2026-11-09, user decision), evidence/pretrain_compiled_contact_20261104/.
reasons.apecss_response: Same APECSS model, case and start from rest as the frozen tables (the 2.4 and 2.6 MHz gates share this case; 2.5 MHz uses it as well); every bubble keeps its own radial state between steps and settles at its own local drive, so the response holds at any pressure and keeps all harmonics. Settling tolerance 1e-3, decay re-measured every 10 calls, ODE tolerance 1e-8 (equal to 1e-10 within 1e-9). Largest force error against a strict settled reference (41 saved states per case): 0.14-0.38% at 20-34 kPa and 2.3% (median 0.4%) at 50 kPa, where the 2.5 MHz table gives 2.4-3.2% and refuses 50 kPa; linear regime 0.16% (2.5 MHz table 5.6%) and 0.09% (2.4 MHz table, exact there, 0.004%). Run time 1.0-1.5x that of the table.
